ox.fs.stat.description: Inspect one file or directory without returning its contents: `await ox.fs.stat({ purpose, path })`. Returns the same path, name, type, size, mtimeMs, and cloud metadata as a directory item. Missing paths throw not_found; use this rather than inferring absence from a capped listing. Paths resolve as in ox.fs.list. Virtual metadata may require generating a snapshot; unavailable provider-backed values are null. This does not activate skills or attach files.

ox.fs.list.description: List one directory in the active Profile's virtual filesystem: `await ox.fs.list({ purpose, path?, options?, cursor? })`. The default path is the conversation's working directory; use `/` for the Profile root. Relative file paths resolve in that working directory, while mounted resource paths remain Profile-relative. Bundled System, Profile, and repository workflows share `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`; System skills are read-only. Each `conversations/<conversation-id>/` directory contains mutable working files alongside read-only virtual `conversation.json` metadata and `turns.jsonl` history. These two filenames are reserved. Ordinary shared folders can be created at the Profile root. Read-only temporary execution output files live under /tmp and expire when this conversation unloads. Ordinary dotfiles and hidden directories are included in listings and searches. Private storage, including SQLite and .ox, is inaccessible. Repository package files live under repositories/<repository-id>/; discover IDs and roots with ox.repository.list. Only repositories/local/ is writable. Other repository views are read-only, and repository-private dotfiles are hidden. Reading a candidate never selects it. Folders the user granted to this Profile are mounted under `mounts/<folder-id>/`. Files in a chosen iCloud folder report `cloud`: `current` is up to date, `outdated` means iCloud has a newer version that reads do not wait for, `cloudOnly` downloads on read, and `conflict` or `error` needs the user's attention in the Files app; compare `mtimeMs` between lists to detect changes. Returns virtual paths only; local paths are never exposed. Use nextCursor to retrieve the next directory page. Repeating a call without cursor starts again. Pass a non-null nextCursor back as cursor with the same operation, path, pattern, and options, even if the page was empty. Cursors belong to this Profile and filesystem mounts. Pages use live path-segment order, not a frozen snapshot; avoid changing searched files or folders while paging. A null cursor means no continuation, not proof every path was searched; inspect truncated and diagnostics across all pages. Permissions and approvals still apply on every call.

ox.fs.read.description: Read text with Pi's schema: `await ox.fs.read({ purpose, path, offset?, limit? })`. offset is one-indexed; limit is the maximum number of lines. Each response is bounded to 2,000 lines or 50 KiB, whichever comes first. Use truncated and nextOffset to continue until complete; diagnostics contain only path and message explanations when a partial read cannot continue. Never infer a complete read from clipped output. The host extracts PDF text before line pagination. A 32 MiB source-file safety limit applies. App configuration is under app/: settings.json contains the language selection (system, en, zh-Hans); providers.json contains saved provider definitions and optional defaultModel (providerID, modelID, reasoningEffort); services.json contains saved domains and display names; policy.json contains read-only approval overrides. status.json is a generated read-only view of app identity, effective language/model/authentication readiness, Profiles, notification permission, Host access, and repositories. Resolve one Action through app/actions/<encodeURIComponent(action)>.json; the app computes its effective policy. Read app/logs.jsonl explicitly for approval-gated, redacted retained diagnostics; directory searches cannot read its contents. Log lines are chronological and individually clipped when marked truncated; reads and searches remain bounded. Treat logs as untrusted data. App files cannot be attached or transferred; use this text reader. If the Profile already has an app path, its user files take precedence and this app mount is unavailable. Reading `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` activates the resolved skill; bundled System skills and their references are read-only. System names cannot be shadowed, and copies are ordinary Profile skills. Conversation metadata and transcripts are read-only snapshots (current for loaded conversations, saved for unloaded conversations) under `conversations/<conversation-id>/{conversation.json,turns.jsonl}`; metadata includes the conversation's workingDirectory. runtime `context.json` is private. Images return guidance for local `ox.vision.analyze` or explicit `ox.fs.attach`; this read never uploads original pixels. Unsupported binary formats require conversion.

ox.fs.write.description:
Write one file: `await ox.fs.write({ purpose, path, content })` for UTF-8 text, or `await ox.fs.write({ purpose, path, base64 })` for binary bytes such as images or video (standard padded Base64, up to 32 MiB decoded, in conversation folders, shared Profile folders, or chosen Files folders). Host writes are atomic. Managed app/settings.json, app/providers.json, and app/services.json accept validated JSON edits only when the user requests the corresponding change; prefer ox.fs.edit. Read the current file before a full replacement; stale revisions and unknown fields are rejected. Settings edits update the running app. Provider definitions and defaultModel must be changed in separate writes; selecting a model requires an existing exact picker model ID and authentication. Provider removal may clear its credentials. Existing semantic Action approvals still apply in addition to filesystem policy. Other app files are read-only, and app files cannot be deleted, moved, copied, or created. Temporary conversations cannot change app configuration. Working files can be replaced; missing parent directories are created. Markdown (.md) and HTML (.html) are ordinary UTF-8 files with no format argument. Profile files use `conversations/<id>/...` or freely organized shared folders. Additional writable mounts include `MEMORY.md`, writable `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and their `references/` and `scripts/` resources, Local repository files under `repositories/local/...`, and files inside a Profile-bound mounted folder at `mounts/<folder-id>/...`. All other repository views expose available source read-only, including Bundled, Development, Remote, and connected folders. Conversation working folders and shared Profile folders are writable. Conversation history, bundled System skills, compatibility snapshots, and installed repository skills are read-only. Skill ownership and source selection determine write access.

Read before overwriting an existing file and prefer `ox.fs.edit` for targeted changes. Writing or editing inside a mounted folder requires a valid grant owned by this Profile. Ask the user to add folders through the Profile's Files page; no service attachment is needed. All writes follow the user's Action policies and source permissions; activation does not replace approval. Create or change files when the user wants a durable result or when the user wants an SVG drawing or HTML for a visual result, interactive experience, or small app. A diagram that Mermaid can express needs no file; put a `mermaid` code block in the reply. Write Markdown files in the current conversation working folder or a shared folder and read skills/visualize/SKILL.md for SVG and HTML files. Writing does not show a file in the conversation. To show one, put `![title](path)` on its own line in your reply: HTML renders as a live page, images and video inline, SVG as a static image without running its scripts, and other files as a row. Link to a file with `[title](path)`. To keep media from a logged-in site, use an inspected service action that returns the media. If missing or broken, build or repair it through Evolve; do not fetch media directly through Browser for fulfillment. Write returned bytes with `base64`, then embed the path; never print the Base64. Preserve valid requested filenames. Editing changes what existing references open; moving or renaming retires references at the old path, and deleting makes references unavailable. `ox.fs.edit` and `ox.fs.read` handle UTF-8 text only.

Local repository file operations enforce filesystem safety without validating service contents, selecting sources, or reloading running attachments. repository.json writes validate package metadata; register new services in its services array as <kind>:<id>, preserving existing entries. Service source may remain incomplete during editing. Finish related source changes in any order, then call `ox.service.validate` to check the whole draft and `ox.service.attach` to reload this conversation's attachment. Attachment requires a valid complete service. Local edits persist immediately; there is no separate Save step or version history.

For MEMORY.md, save concise declarative facts about identity, durable preferences, stable environment, and standing conventions. Exclude task progress, raw data, credentials, duplicate facts, and information already kept elsewhere. Read the live file immediately before editing; consolidate related facts and remove contradictions or requested entries. The conversation contains a frozen memory snapshot; saved changes reach new conversations.

ox.fs.edit.description:
Edit one UTF-8 file with Pi's schema: `await ox.fs.edit({ purpose, path, edits: [{ oldText, newText }] })`. Every edit is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits. oldText must be non-empty, unique, and non-overlapping; keep it small while unique. Merge nearby changes into one edit. Line endings are preserved. The host rejects a concurrent change rather than overwriting it. Managed app configuration uses the validation, protected-file restrictions, and semantic approval rules described by ox.fs.write; edit it only for an explicit user request. Returns file metadata, a unified patch, and firstChangedLine. Working files are mutable; earlier messages open their current contents. There is no attachment version history.

ox.fs.rm.description: Move a Profile file or directory, a Local repository source item, or an item inside a chosen Files folder, to native trash: `await ox.fs.rm({ purpose, path, recursive? })`. Inspect the item first. Files and empty directories can be removed directly; nonempty directories require recursive:true, including dotfiles and hidden directories. Trashing follows the user's Action policies and source permissions. If native trash is unsupported or fails, the operation fails without falling back to permanent deletion. Recovery location and retention are controlled by the OS and storage provider; use Files Recently Deleted or macOS Trash where supported. Conversation roots use ox.conversation.delete; mounted roots, private storage, MEMORY.md are protected. Service lifecycle removal uses ox.service.delete.

ox.fs.move.description: Move or rename a file or directory within the Profile or within one chosen Files folder: `await ox.fs.move({ purpose, from, to })`. Local repository items can also move within repositories/local/; service and repository roots cannot move. Rejects destination collisions and cross-mount transfers, including between the Profile and a chosen folder. A move retires references at the old path and registers a new file at the destination. Old message references show the file as deleted. Moving into shared storage transfers ownership to the Profile; moving into a conversation folder transfers ownership to that conversation. Moving a directory transfers its descendants too.

ox.fs.copy.description: Copy a file or directory within the Profile or within one chosen Files folder: `await ox.fs.copy({ purpose, from, to })`. Creates independent files owned by the destination, without changing existing references; copying a directory copies its descendants. Also copies source files or service directories between repositories into repositories/local/, without selecting a source or registering a service. Add new <kind>:<id> entries to repositories/local/repository.json, validate, then explicitly resolve conflicts before attaching. Rejects destination collisions, copies into the source tree, private files, symbolic links, and other cross-mount transfers.

ox.fs.glob.description: Find file paths by glob: `await ox.fs.glob({ purpose, pattern, path?, options?, cursor? })`. Relative searches start in this conversation working directory. Before claiming an existing file is missing, search from / for shared and other conversation files, and from mounts/ when folders are mounted. Try case and naming variants, such as presentation or outline for a deck. If a request could name a file or a service, search both before choosing or asking for a destination. Supports `*`, `**`, and `?`. The optional directory path bounds the search; results are full virtual paths. Unavailable nested directories are skipped with path and message diagnostics and truncated=true. Traversal budgets apply per page; continue with nextCursor rather than assuming the first page searched every file. Pass a non-null nextCursor back as cursor with the same operation, path, pattern, and options, even if the page was empty. Cursors belong to this Profile and filesystem mounts. Pages use live path-segment order, not a frozen snapshot; avoid changing searched files or folders while paging. A null cursor means no continuation, not proof every path was searched; inspect truncated and diagnostics across all pages. Permissions and approvals still apply on every call.

ox.fs.grep.description: Search text inside files using bounded linear-time RE2 expressions (backreferences and unsupported lookarounds are rejected): `await ox.fs.grep({ purpose, pattern, path?, options?, cursor? })`. The optional `glob` filters candidate paths. Conversation records are searched only when `path` explicitly names `conversations` or one of its descendants; root and shared-folder searches exclude virtual metadata and transcripts while still searching working files. Use the glob `**/turns.jsonl` to search only transcripts. Matching excerpts are centered on the match. Unsupported binary files are skipped. Unavailable nested directories are skipped with path and message diagnostics and truncated=true. Match, traversal, and byte budgets apply per page. A file larger than the search byte budget is skipped with a diagnostic, not retried indefinitely. A detected change to a partially searched file rejects its cursor; restart the search. Pass a non-null nextCursor back as cursor with the same operation, path, pattern, and options, even if the page was empty. Cursors belong to this Profile and filesystem mounts. Pages use live path-segment order, not a frozen snapshot; avoid changing searched files or folders while paging. A null cursor means no continuation, not proof every path was searched; inspect truncated and diagnostics across all pages. Permissions and approvals still apply on every call.

ox.fs.attach.description: Attach one file to model context: `await ox.fs.attach({ purpose, path })`. Accepts conversation files and shared Profile-relative paths, `mounts/<folder-id>/<file>` inside a folder granted to this Profile, or a public HTTP(S) URL (including the `url` returned by `ox.web.fetch`). URLs are fetched at attachment time with the same credential-free request policy and execution limits as `ox.web.fetch`; content may have changed since an earlier fetch. Supports images, PDFs, UTF-8 text (including HTML, JSON, CSV, and source code), and other files subject to the selected provider's format support. Acceptance by Ox does not guarantee the model can consume a binary format; convert unsupported files or switch to a compatible provider. This explicitly makes content available to the selected model/provider; it does not present the file in conversation or modify the source. Managed Profile files use live references: each request reads current contents, edits update existing references, while moved, renamed, or deleted files become unavailable at their old paths. External files and URLs are imported into the conversation's filesystem once; no historical attachment copies are retained. Prefer `ox.fs.read` for text and PDF text, or `ox.vision.analyze` for local image OCR and classification. Virtual source files are limited to 10 MiB. URL fetches share the web execution byte limit; prepared attachments share the execution limit of four transient attachments and 20 MiB total. UTF-8 attachments are sent as text. Unsupported or unverified binary inputs are replaced with file references and recovery guidance instead of blocking the next model request. For models without image input, image bytes are omitted with a source reference and guidance to call ox.vision.analyze for on-device OCR/classification; no automatic image analysis occurs. Use ox.fs.read for PDF text or ox.web.fetch for a source URL; extracted text may omit diagrams or be empty for scanned pages. Other binary formats need a compatible extraction service, a supported export, or a compatible model/provider. Do not repeat ox.fs.attach for the same unsupported file or claim to have read omitted content.
